name: Nature, City and Working Memory Restoration
description: Faithful replication of van Oordt, Ouwehand & Paas (2023), "Restorative Effects of Observing Natural and Urban Scenery after Working Memory Depletion", Int. J. Environ. Res. Public Health 20:188. Participants give gender, age and education and are assigned at random to a nature, urban or control group. All first do a digital Trier Mental Challenge Test for about 10 minutes (arithmetic answered with on-screen buttons within 5 s, +1/−1 points, difficulty steps at 36, 40, 45 and 50 points) to deplete working memory. The nature group then views the paper's 30 pictures of a Dutch park and the urban group its 30 pictures of Dutch residential streets, 7.5 s each; the control group sees no pictures. Finally everyone does a forward and a backward digit span test (up to 14 trials, two sets per trial, stop after two failed sets). Analysis as in the paper: one-way ANOVA of digit span across the three groups. Pictures: the paper's own photographs (Appendices A and B, CC BY 4.0), used with credit; the template is removed if the authors object. Differences from the original study: (1) runs as a web page instead of Inquisit; (2) the paper does not list the arithmetic problems per difficulty level, so the five levels are our own (single-digit addition up to two-digit × one-digit multiplication), and answers are confirmed with an OK button; (3) the digit span starts at two digits per set and shows one digit per second, which the paper does not state; (4) pictures are shown in the appendix order; (5) if the page is reloaded during a task, that task starts again.
author: van Oordt, Ouwehand & Paas

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I have read the information above and agree to take part voluntarily. I know I can stop at any time.

elements.name: condition
elements.title: Experimental condition
elements.description: Assigned at random with equal probability: 'nature' (view 30 park pictures), 'urban' (view 30 residential-street pictures) or 'control' (no pictures).

elements.name: tmct
elements.title: Mental arithmetic task (depletion)
elements.description: Digital Trier Mental Challenge Test, about 10 minutes: arithmetic problems answered with on-screen buttons 0–9 within 5 seconds; +1 point when correct, −1 when wrong or too late; difficulty goes up one step at 36, 40, 45 and 50 points and down again below them. Only used to deplete working memory. Value: {points, maxLevel, problems, correct}.

elements.name: picture_viewing
elements.title: Picture viewing
elements.description: Nature and urban groups: the 30 pictures of their condition, each shown for 7.5 s (about 4 minutes), in the order of the paper's appendix. shown = the pictures viewed. Control group: value 'none'.

elements.name: digit_span
elements.title: Digit span (working memory capacity)
elements.description: Forward then backward digit span, up to 14 trials each; trial n presents two sets of n+1 digits (one digit per second) and the participant reproduces them with on-screen buttons (backward: in reverse order). The next trial starts when at least one set of the trial is correct; the test stops when both sets of a trial are wrong. Value: {forward_sets, backward_sets, total_sets, forward_span, backward_span}. Analysis as in the paper: one-way ANOVA of digit span (forward, backward, total) across nature, urban and control groups.
